full_text_en:
Shanxi Anye Group Co., Ltd. v. Taiyuan Municipal People's Government, Shanxi Province — dispute over decision to收回 state-owned land use rights

Ruling Summary

Where there is expropriation, there must be compensation; without compensation, there is no expropriation. Expropriation compensation shall follow the principle of timely compensation and the principle of fair compensation. Before the compensation issue is resolved through legally prescribed procedures, the expropriated person has the right to refuse to surrender the house and land.

Supreme People's Court Administrative Judgment

(2016) Zui Gao Fa Xing Zai Zi No. 80

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Shanxi Anye Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 50 Shuangta West Street, Taiyuan, Shanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Wei Baolin, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Wang Junjie, lawyer, Shanxi Huike Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Pan Xuelin, staff member, Shanxi Anye Group Co., Ltd.

Respondent to Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Taiyuan Municipal People's Government, Shanxi Province, domiciled at No. 69 Xinjian Road, Taiyuan, Shanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Geng Yanbo, Mayor of the City.

Agent ad litem: Meng Xuejun, staff member, Legal Affairs Office of Taiyuan Municipal People's Government, Shanxi Province.

Agent ad litem: Guo Jiadong, staff member, Taiyuan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources, Shanxi Province.

The Applicant for Retrial, Shanxi Anye Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Anye Company), filed a dispute against the Respondent to Retrial, Taiyuan Municipal People's Government, Shanxi Province (hereinafter referred to as Taiyuan Municipal Government), concerning the decision to recover state-owned land use rights. Dissatisfied with the administrative judgment (2015) Jin Xing Zhong Zi No. 50 rendered by the Shanxi High People's Court, Anye Company applied to this Court for retrial. After a hearing and examination, this Court rendered an administrative ruling (2015) Xing Jian Zi No. 2102 on May 24, 2016, deciding to bring the case up for retrial. After the retrial was initiated, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, composed of Presiding Judge Geng Baojian, Acting Judge Li Weihua, and Acting Judge Zhou Mi, and conducted a public trial of the case. Wang Junjie and Pan Xuelin, agents ad litem of Anye Company, and Meng Xuejun and Guo Jiadong, agents ad litem of Taiyuan Municipal Government, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The trial is now concluded.

The courts of first instance and second instance found the following main facts: Anye Company successively obtained the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" for No. 162 Shuangta West Street in April 2004 and October 2005, and obtained the "House Property Ownership Certificate" on March 1, 2006. For the purpose of implementing the road construction and renovation of Jiefang South Road and Changzhi Road, Taiyuan Municipal Government issued on April 4, 2014, the "Notice of Taiyuan Municipal People's Government on the Recovery of Part of the State-owned Land Use Rights South of Yingze Street and North of Zhongxin Street in Connection with the Implementation of the Road Construction and Renovation of Jiefang South Road and Changzhi Road" (hereinafter referred to as the "Notice"), which was published in the "Taiyuan Daily" on April 10, 2014, and on the land recovery column of the website of the Taiyuan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources, Shanxi Province. The Notice informed relevant units and households that the municipal government had decided to recover the state-owned land use rights of 776.85 mu of land involving 87 units in connection with the road construction of Jiefang South Road and Changzhi Road. Units and households involved were required to bring relevant land documents to the Taiyuan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources within 15 days from the date of publication of the Notice to complete the cancellation procedures for land use rights; if they failed to return the documents within the time limit, the rights would be cancelled. The Notice stated that the areas of the two plots of land involved with Anye Company were 7.77 square meters and 741.73 square meters respectively, totaling 749.5 square meters. Anye Company, dissatisfied with the Notice, filed this lawsuit, requesting that the act of Taiyuan Municipal Government in recovering its state-owned land use rights be revoked according to law.

The courts of first instance and second instance found that: Taiyuan Municipal Government issued the Notice on April 4, 2014, deciding to recover the state-owned land use rights of 776.85 mu of land involving 87 units in connection with the road construction and renovation of Jiefang South Road and Changzhi Road, with clear northern and southern boundaries, involved units, and recovered land areas. The recovery of state-owned land within the notified area was for the purpose of implementing road construction and renovation projects to realize urban planning, which falls under the use of land for public interest. According to legal provisions, upon approval by the competent authority, the people's government may recover state-owned land use rights. Before the issuance of the Notice, the relevant units went through the procedures for land use planning and reported to Taiyuan Municipal Government for approval, and the recovery procedure complied with legal provisions. According to the Land Administration Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Land Administration Law), state-owned land recovered according to law may be directly handled for cancellation of registration. Therefore, the content of the Notice regarding the cancellation of land use rights did not violate legal provisions. Taiyuan Municipal Government's recovery of Anye Company's lawfully obtained state-owned land use rights shall be compensated according to law. The Notice also clarified that the compensation matters related to the demolition and relocation involved in the recovery of the above state-owned land use rights would be handled according to relevant regulations and in accordance with the law. After the Notice was published on April 10, 2014, the project was decided to be suspended on May 7, so compensation work was not actually carried out. Anye Company's claim that Taiyuan Municipal Government must implement compensation before issuing the Notice had no factual or legal basis. Accordingly, the court of first instance rendered a judgment dismissing Anye Company's claim to revoke the administrative expropriation decision in Taiyuan Municipal Government's Notice No. (2014) 018. Anye Company, dissatisfied, appealed, and the court of second instance rendered a judgment dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

In its application for retrial to this Court, the Applicant for Retrial, Anye Company, requested that the final judgment of the Shanxi High People's Court be revoked. The reasons were: First, Taiyuan Municipal Government's direct decision to recover the land use rights without settling compensation matters constituted a procedural violation. Second, the subject for recovering state-owned land use rights is the land administrative department of the people's government; Taiyuan Municipal Government, as a prefecture-level people's government, directly made the decision to recover state-owned land use rights, which constituted an abuse of administrative power. Third, the recovery of state-owned land use rights must comply with the overall land use plan and the overall urban plan, and the planning procedures must include the opinions of experts and the public through demonstration meetings, hearings, or other means, and modifications to the plan must be approved according to legal procedures. In this case, Taiyuan Municipal Government directly decided to recover the state-owned land use rights without the road renovation planning procedures being completed according to law, which was a procedural violation. Fourth, laws and regulations such as the Urban Real Estate Administration Law of the PRC and the Interim Regulations on the Assignment and Transfer of the Right to Use State-owned Land in Cities and Towns all provide that under special circumstances and for the needs of social public interest, the state may recover land use rights in advance according to legal procedures. Taiyuan Municipal Government's land recovery act clearly did not meet the "special circumstances" stipulated by law; it has been two years since the decision, but the road renovation project has not started, which obviously violates the basic principles of law-based administration and reasonable administration in China. Fifth, according to the principle of due process and relevant legal provisions, before making a decision affecting the vital interests of citizens, legal persons, or other organizations, the state administrative organ shall inform the counterpart of the facts, reasons, and basis for the decision, and hear the statements and defenses of the parties involved; after making the administrative decision, it shall serve the written decision on the administrative counterpart. From beginning to end, Taiyuan Municipal Government did not serve a written decision on the recovery of state-owned land use rights to Anye Company, nor did it inform Anye Company of any facts, reasons, or basis for the decision to recover the land use rights, nor did it hear Anye Company's statements and defenses. Instead, it only published the Notice on the land recovery column of the website of the Taiyuan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources, announcing the area of 749.5 square meters of Anye Company's land to be recovered (with unclear four boundaries). In summary, Taiyuan Municipal Government's administrative act was clearly procedurally improper and constituted illegal administration. It was improper for the lower courts to dismiss Anye Company's claims, and the judgments should be revoked according to law.

The Respondent to Retrial, Taiyuan Municipal Government, argued in its defense: According to Article 58 of the Land Administration Law, where land is needed for public interest, the land administrative department, upon approval by the competent authority, may recover state-owned land use rights. Taiyuan Municipal Government's decision to recover state-owned land use rights was made by a qualified subject within statutory powers. Taiyuan Municipal Government issued the Notice regarding the recovery of land use rights in the road renovation area and published it in the media; the decision to recover state-owned land use rights had clear facts and legal procedures. According to the Measures for Land Registration, state-owned land recovered according to law may be directly handled for cancellation of registration; Taiyuan Municipal Government's requirement that relevant units and households, including Anye Company, complete the cancellation procedures for land use rights within 15 days from the date of publication, and that if they failed to return the documents, the rights would be cancelled, complied with legal provisions. The request was to dismiss Anye Company's retrial application.

During the hearing and trial examination of this case before this Court, the parties had no objection to the main facts found by the lower courts, and this Court affirms them. However, during the retrial trial of this case, the Respondent to Retrial, Taiyuan Municipal Government, stated that the lower courts found that "after the Notice was published on April 10, 2014, the project was decided and announced to be suspended on May 7," which was a fact found by the courts of first and second instance based on relevant evidence. Although relevant newspapers have publicly reported the suspension of the project, Taiyuan Municipal Government and relevant functional departments have not made a written decision on the suspension.

During the trial of this case, upon the request of this Court, the parties negotiated multiple times to resolve the dispute but reached no agreement.

This Court finds: Where there is expropriation, there must be compensation; without compensation, there is no expropriation. For the needs of public interest such as safeguarding national security, promoting national economic development, and social progress, the state may recover state-owned land use rights according to law, and may also expropriate houses on state-owned land owned by units or individuals; however, the state must provide timely and fair compensation to the expropriated person, and cannot only expropriate without compensation or unreasonably delay compensation. Generally, an expropriation decision should include specific compensation content. If, due to evaluation, negotiation between parties, or other special reasons, the expropriation decision does not include compensation content, the expropriation authority shall, within a reasonable time after the decision takes effect, promptly resolve the compensation issue by signing an expropriation compensation agreement or making an expropriation compensation decision. Expropriation compensation shall follow the principle of timely compensation and the principle of fair compensation. When the state needs to use land and houses in urban areas for public interest, the city or county people's government shall generally follow the procedures and methods provided in the Regulations on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-owned Land (hereinafter referred to as the Expropriation and Compensation Regulations), and, in accordance with the spirit of the Measures for the Assessment of Expropriation of Houses on State-owned Land and the Regulations for the Valuation of Urban Land, engage a professional real estate price assessment institution to conduct on-site surveys and evaluate the value of the expropriated real estate based on factors such as location and usage that affect the value of the expropriated real estate and local market conditions, comprehensively selecting assessment methods such as market approach, income approach, cost approach, and hypothetical development approach to reasonably determine the assessment results, and provide compensation on that basis. If the compensation to the owner of a house on state-owned land already includes compensation for the state-owned land use rights, the holder of the land use rights for the simultaneously recovered state-owned land will not be separately compensated. The time point for assessing the value of the expropriated real estate shall generally be the date of publication of the expropriation decision or the date on which the expropriation decision is served on the expropriated person. If the expropriating authority causes unreasonable delay in the expropriation compensation issue, and the price of the expropriated real estate significantly increases, the expropriated person is entitled to demand that the market price at the time the expropriation compensation decision is made or the expropriation compensation agreement is signed be used as the compensation base. If the expropriated person has objections to the compensation amount or other content determined by the expropriation compensation decision or the expropriation compensation agreement, they may file an administrative lawsuit according to law. If the expropriation authority completes relevant procedures such as deposit in accordance with the law and notifies the expropriated person in writing of the collection of compensation funds, use of resettlement houses, etc., and the expropriated person refuses to collect without legally justified reasons, the expropriation authority will not bear compensation liability for the increase in the price of the expropriated property during the litigation period.

In this case, due to the need for road construction and renovation projects, Taiyuan Municipal Government and relevant functional departments may recover state-owned land use rights according to law, but they must follow legal procedures and steps and timely resolve the compensation issue according to law. In this case, when Taiyuan Municipal Government recovered the 749.5 square meters of land for which Anye Company had use rights, it neither heard Anye Company's statements and defenses, nor determined the four boundaries of the land involved, and, in particular, has not yet provided any compensation to Anye Company, which fails to comply with the spirit of Article 58 of the Land Administration Law, Article 42, Paragraph 3 of the Real Right Law of the PRC, Article 6 of the Urban Real Estate Administration Law of the PRC, and Articles 8, 13, and 27 of the Expropriation and Compensation Regulations, and should be revoked according to law. However, considering that the relevant road construction and renovation project is indeed for the needs of public interest, in accordance with Article 74, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the administrative act of Taiyuan Municipal Government in recovering 749.5 square meters of state-owned land use rights of Anye Company by means of the Notice should be confirmed as illegal. In the future, if the road construction and renovation actually uses the corresponding land of Anye Company, Anye Company has the right to claim compensation based on the market value of the land at the time of actual use; Anye Company also has the right to demand compensation before relocation, and before the compensation issue is resolved according to law, Anye Company has the right to refuse to surrender the land. In summary, in accordance with Article 74, Paragraph 1, Item 1 and Article 89, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, and Article 78 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. Revoke the administrative judgment (2015) Jin Xing Zhong Zi No. 50 of the Shanxi High People's Court and the administrative judgment (2014) Bing Xing Chu Zi No. 43 of the Taiyuan Intermediate People's Court, Shanxi Province;

2. Confirm that the administrative act of the Respondent to Retrial, Taiyuan Municipal People's Government, Shanxi Province, in the "Notice of Taiyuan Municipal People's Government on the Recovery of Part of the State-owned Land Use Rights South of Yingze Street and North of Zhongxin Street in Connection with the Implementation of the Road Construction and Renovation of Jiefang South Road and Changzhi Road" (No. [2014] 018), concerning the recovery of 749.5 square meters of state-owned land use rights of Shanxi Anye Group Co., Ltd., is illegal.

The total case acceptance fee for the first instance and second instance is RMB 100, which shall be borne by the Respondent to Retrial, Taiyuan Municipal People's Government, Shanxi Province.

This judgment is final.

Acting Judge: Li Weihua
